# Term definition

## Acronym soup

![source: Duck AI](assets/01_ntn_building_blocks.jpeg)

## NTN context

Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) extend mobile connectivity through spaceborne or airborne platforms such as satellites and high-altitude systems, while reusing major parts of the 3GPP cellular architecture.[^1]

## Gateway

A **Gateway** is the ground segment node that connects the satellite or other NTN access segment to the terrestrial core network and transport network.[^1]

In practice, it terminates feeder links and forwards user and control traffic between the NTN payload and the mobile network infrastructure.[^1]

## gNB

A **gNB** is the 5G New Radio base station node defined for NG-RAN.[^2]

In NTN deployments, the gNB may be located on the ground or split across ground and space segments depending on the architecture.[^1][^2]

## NR

**NR** means New Radio, the 5G radio access technology standardized by 3GPP.[^2]

In NTN, NR is adapted so 5G air-interface procedures can operate over satellite channels with larger delay, Doppler, and coverage footprints than terrestrial cells.[^1]

## eNB

An **eNB** is the E-UTRAN NodeB, the LTE base station used in 4G radio access networks.[^3]

In NTN discussions, eNB usually appears when the system is based on LTE/E-UTRA rather than 5G NR.[^1][^3]

## 5GC

The **5GC** is the 5G Core network, which provides core functions such as access and mobility management, session management, policy control, and user-plane connectivity for 5G systems.[^4]

For NTN, 5GC can serve NR-based satellite access similarly to terrestrial 5G, with NTN-specific adaptations handled mainly in the access side and procedures.[^1][^4]

## EPC

The **EPC** is the Evolved Packet Core, the core network architecture used with LTE/EPS systems.[^5]

In NTN architectures based on LTE, EPC plays the same core-network role that 5GC plays for 5G systems.[^1][^5]

## Relationship map

- **NR + gNB + 5GC**: typical 5G system stack in NTN.[^1][^2][^4]
- **LTE/E-UTRA + eNB + EPC**: typical 4G system stack in NTN.[^1][^3][^5]
- **Gateway**: bridge between NTN access infrastructure and the terrestrial network/core.[^1]


[^1]: 3GPP TR 38.821, *Solutions for NR to support non-terrestrial networks (NTN)*, [3GPP portal](https://portal.3gpp.org/desktopmodules/Specifications/SpecificationDetails.aspx?specificationId=3525).
[^2]: 3GPP, *Release 17 description; Summary of Rel-17 work items*, [3GPP portal](https://www.3gpp.org/DynaReport/Rel-17.htm).
[^3]: ETSI / 3GPP TS 36.300, *E-UTRA and E-UTRAN; Overall description*, [ETSI catalog](https://standards.iteh.ai/catalog/standards/etsi/dfd0e7ef-1f52-45d8-a6bf-df9ef8d3dcef/etsi-ts-136-300-v16-12-0-2023-01).
[^4]: 3GPP TS 23.501, *System architecture for the 5G System (5GS)*, [3GPP portal](https://portal.3gpp.org/desktopmodules/Specifications/SpecificationDetails.aspx?specificationId=3144).
[^5]: 3GPP TS 23.401, *General Packet Radio Service (GPRS) enhancements for E-UTRAN access*, [3GPP portal](https://portal.3gpp.org/desktopmodules/Specifications/SpecificationDetails.aspx?specificationId=1385).
